subject: english_literature
question_text: Copy and complete the following paragraph about the theme of the play in pairs:
answer_text: The play deals with a kind and charitable Bishop who is always ready to lend a helping hand to anyone in distress. A convict breaks into the Bishop’s house and is fed and warmed. The benevolence of the Bishop somewhat confounds the convict, but, when he sees the silver candlesticks, he steals them, and runs away. However, he is arrested and brought back. He expects to go back to jail, but the Bishop informs the police they are a gift. The convict is moved by this kindness of the Bishop and before he leaves he seeks the priest’s blessing.
final_answer: The convict is moved by this kindness of the Bishop and before he leaves he seeks the priest’s blessing.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the play's themes and character motivations.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What does the convict mean when he says, 'Give me food or I’ll stick my knife in you both and help myself.'?
answer_text: The convict is expressing desperation and a threat, indicating that he feels he has no choice but to resort to violence if his basic needs are not met.
final_answer: Thus, the statement reflects his dire situation and the lengths he might go to for survival.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of character motivations and context.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What does the convict mean when he says, '__________they have made me what I am, they have made me a thief. God curse them all.'?
answer_text: The convict is blaming others for his circumstances, suggesting that societal injustices have forced him into a life of crime.
final_answer: Therefore, he feels resentment towards those he believes have wronged him.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves interpretation of character's feelings and societal critique.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What does the convict mean when he asks, 'Why the devil are you kind to me? What do you want?'?
answer_text: The convict is expressing suspicion towards the bishop's kindness, questioning the motives behind it.
final_answer: This reflects his distrust and the impact of his past experiences on his perception of others.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of character's emotional state and past.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What does the convict mean when he says, 'I − I − didn’t believe there was any good in the world…but somehow I − I − know you’re good, and − and it’s a queer thing to ask, but could you, would you bless me before I go?'?
answer_text: The convict is expressing a newfound hope and vulnerability, recognizing goodness in the bishop despite his bleak outlook on life.
final_answer: This moment signifies a turning point for him, showing his desire for redemption.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves deeper emotional understanding and character development.

parts.part_text: Do you think the Bishop was right in selling the salt-cellars? Why/why not?
parts.answer_text: No, the Bishop was not right in selling the salt-cellars. His own economic condition was not good and he should have asked for Persome’s opinion before he sold the cellars, which belonged to her too. From another point of view the Bishop was right in selling the salt-cellars as he wanted to give the money he got from selling the cellars to Mere Gringoire who could not give rent to the landlord on time and was about to face eviction. The Bishop was very broadminded as he could empathise with the condition of Mere Gringoire and chose to do away with the salt cellars. The Bishop felt that one could eat salt out of china as well.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, the Bishop's decision can be seen as both right and wrong depending on the perspective.

parts.part_text: Why does Persome feel the people pretend to be sick?
parts.answer_text: Persome is protective and wishes to maintain the household. She is pained to see that the entire humanity is turning upon them for charity and benevolence. She feels people like Marie’s mother pretend to be sick and take undue advantage of the Bishop.
parts.final_answer: Persome believes that some people exploit the Bishop's kindness.

parts.part_text: Who was Jeanette? What was the cause of her death?
parts.answer_text: Jeanette was the convict’s wife. She died due to illness and starvation.
parts.final_answer: Jeanette's death was caused by illness and starvation.

parts.part_text: The convict says, “I am too old a bird to be caught with chaff.” What does he mean by this statement?
parts.answer_text: The convict has suffered, he is embittered, he is experienced. So he couldn’t be tricked. He ordered the Bishop to stay put because he couldn’t trust anyone not to report to the police and get him arrested.
parts.final_answer: The convict means that he is wise enough not to be deceived easily.

parts.part_text: Why was the convict sent to prison? What was the punishment given to him?
parts.answer_text: The convict was sent to prison for stealing a loaf of bread. He was sentenced to ten years in a prison hulk.
parts.final_answer: He was punished for stealing food to feed his starving wife.

parts.part_text: Do you think the punishment given to the convict was justified? Why/why not? Why is the convict eager to reach Paris?
parts.answer_text: The punishment given to the convict was not justified. It is too inhuman for someone who was caught stealing just to feed his sick wife. He was guilty of stealing only to feed his wife who was dying of starvation. But they showed him no mercy and treated him like a beast. They chained him like a wild animal, lashed him like a hound and fed him filth. He was covered with vermin and had to sleep on boards. This kind of treatment is inhuman and not justified. The convict is eager to reach Paris because it was a big city and the Police would never be able to find him there.
parts.final_answer: The convict's eagerness to reach Paris stems from the hope of escaping his past.

parts.part_text: Before leaving, the convict asks the Bishop to bless him. What brought about this change in him?
parts.answer_text: The Bishop’s benevolent, kind and caring attitude had brought about a change in the convict. That is why before leaving for Paris, he asks the Bishop to bless him.
parts.final_answer: The convict's change is due to the Bishop's kindness.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of character motivations and moral dilemmas.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What is the turning point in the convict's life?
answer_text: The Convict, when was caught and brought to the Bishop’s house, was asked to be released by the Bishop saying that he is a friend to him. The Bishop also gives him his mother’s only memory i.e. candle-sticks. This entire incidence makes convict believe that there still exists humanity. This is the turning point in the convict’s life.
final_answer: This is the turning point in the convict’s life.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of character development and thematic elements.
